commits.message: Merge the latest end-to-end commits into colll78/canonical-v1-watcher-l1-source-checkpoint
Mark the delivered lint rules, obligation tests, test-environment skill and compose derivation in the hardening plan

Give exact-point recovery captures the ledger-scan deadline

Ogmios has no address index, so the state-queue capture that the expired
intent release and the signed-header recovery take at the history
checkpoint walks the whole UTxO set. Both ran under the 30 s per-request
source timeout. On preprod one such scan takes about 13 s alone and about
36 s when three clients of the same node scan at once, as happens when
the DA members and the node start together, so the capture timed out and
the history owner never became ready.

Both captures now use the same scan deadline as the first-start capture,
moved next to the snapshot reader. The history lease keeps renewing from
the follower's heartbeats while a recovery capture runs. The capture
failure now carries its cause in the message; the log previously showed
only "capture failed".

Document the Midgard lint rules and tag the rules they enforce

docs/agents/lint-rules.md lists each rule with the ruling behind it, its
blind spots and the baseline workflow. The localUPLCEval, validity-window,
exact-fee and command-placement rules in the agent docs now carry the
eslint tags, and the enforcement-tag check knows the new rules, so a
[review] tag on a rule they enforce is reported as an under-claim.

Leave localUPLCEval to the workspace lint rule in the fault-proof limit scan

The limit-escape scan checked localUPLCEval in midgard-fault-proofs only.
The midgard/local-uplc-eval lint rule now checks it in every package with
the same markers, so the scan drops that kind and keeps the publication
and transaction-limit checks.

Check owner rulings with a local ESLint plugin and a shrink-only baseline

The demo workspace's ESLint config now loads eslint-plugin-midgard from
demo/scripts/lib, with eight rules that each end their message with how
to fix the violation:

- locale-compare-explicit-locale: localeCompare without a locale
- local-uplc-eval: localUPLCEval set to anything but the literal true,
  outside the unpublishable-diagnostic markers
- fault-proof-reference-scripts-only: inline attach in the fault-proof
  source trees
- apply-params-through-blueprint: raw parameter application outside the
  blueprint shape guard, and renamed imports of it
- exact-fee-no-change-output: setMinFee without a completion in the same
  function that turns coin selection off
- scoped-utxo-override: an overrideUTxOs pin with no later
  clearUTxOOverride on the same receiver
- valid-from-wall-clock-margin: a validity lower bound from the wall
  clock without a 30-second margin
- node-cli-operator-commands-only: test, demo or bench commands in the
  operator binary

Violations that predate a rule are listed in baseline.json by rule, file
and line text, each file entry with a reason, and do not fail the lint.
A listed line that no longer occurs fails it, and prune-baseline.mjs only
removes sites. The plugin's test lints each rule's fixtures and requires
the reported lines to equal the ruleid lines, fails a rule without
ruleid and ok cases, checks every rule is an error in the config, and
refuses baseline entries without a reason or for missing rules or files.
Map each validator and fault-proof family to its passing and failing emulator scenarios

Replace a missed signed commit and reconcile to whichever commit lands

A signed commit and its replacement both spend the same state-queue tail
node, and the state queue appends only onto a node with an empty next, so
at most one of them can land. The node no longer holds a missed commit
until a coverage proof shows it can never land. Once the authenticated
head reaches the commit's exclusive TTL with the tail's next still empty,
or another header has taken the tail, the history owner abandons the
journal under a replacement digest, reopens its members, removes its
local finalization job, releases the lease and moves the native root and
SQL marker back to the base. The commit worker then builds a new commit
on the same tail.

If a rollback shows an earlier replaced commit landed after all, the owner
revives that journal, abandons the active replacement, re-takes the
revived journal's members and restores the candidate root. Only journals
abandoned by replacement are ever revived; blocks removed by a state-queue
correction are not. Reviving over a replacement that has already been
locally finalized is a fatal integrity error raised before anything is
written. When the tail node itself has been removed by a correction, the
correction path owns the journal and the release defers to it. The
confirmation workers defer every signed intent to the history owner
instead of refusing replacement.

The coverage proof requirement and the intent retention hold are removed.

Also included are the rewind review fixes: a rejected transaction is fully
reversed when a correction re-includes a block (admission, address history
and ledger receipts), the rollback check runs before a revoke and its
integrity error is fatal, a payload of an abandoned or removed block is no
longer owed to the DA committee, blocked pending reconciliation backs off
and warns periodically, and the SQL marker update is a compare-and-swap.

Known open items: a tail spent and then merged away is treated as removed
by a correction (defer) and a commit that landed and was merged before the
owner saw it waits; both can wedge a multi-operator deployment. A
replacement also terminally rejects pending transactions that spend the
replaced block's deposit outputs.
Check every fraud-proof category id written in the repository against the catalogue

Add a local-test-environment skill

What a checkout needs before its suites can run, verified against the tree:
the shared test Postgres on 127.0.0.1:5433 from scripts/start-test-postgres.sh
with synchronous_commit on, the per-worktree test-database prefix and
MIDGARD_TEST_DATABASE_PREFIX, which packages' pretest builds dist and why
(plain node resolves the workspace packages to dist, vitest to src), the
blueprint stamp guard and its rebuild command, and running the operator
compose stack from a linked worktree. scripts/doctor.mjs is its entry point.

docs/agents/verification.md now points at the skill instead of repeating the
Postgres and test-database notes, and the skill gets a line budget.

Give each worktree's operator compose stack its own project and ports

The operator compose files in demo/midgard-node took their project name from
the directory and published fixed host ports and fixed container names
(prometheus, loki, promtail, grafana), so a second checkout's stack took over
the first one's containers or failed on its ports.

Every host port is now a variable whose default is today's value, and the
container names take an optional prefix. scripts/operator-compose.sh runs
docker compose with values derived from scripts/lib/worktree-identity.mjs: the
main checkout gets nothing, so its project, container names and ports stay
exactly as before; a linked worktree gets project midgard-node-<hash>,
prefixed container names and its own block of 100 host ports from
20000 + 100 * slot. A block rather than phase 4's single offset, because these
defaults differ by multiples of 10 (12788/12798, 3100/3200) and one offset per
worktree would land one worktree's port on another's. A value already set in
the environment or the env file compose reads, or -p, wins.

The four host-port lines in .env.example are commented out: set there, a copy
in a worktree would pin the historical ports and defeat the derivation. No
code reads them inside the container.

operator-compose.test.mjs renders the real compose files and proves the main
checkout keeps today's names and ports, two linked worktrees get different
projects and disjoint ports, and an explicit setting wins; midgard-node-ci runs
it in the operator compose job.
Run CI's full Aiken suite through the fail-closed guard and lint for a bare aiken check
